A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T-REGS research and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic point-cloud experiments, SSL and image-text retrieval evaluations, and ablations in Sections 4.2–5 and Appendices E–F. These include original T-REGS results alongside literature-derived baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic experiments, T-REGS benchmark and retrieval results, and appendix ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: The MST-length objective, soft sphere constraint, standalone and auxiliary SSL objectives, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Figure 1 is restyled without changing the depicted procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic point-cloud scenarios, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-100/1k, and Flickr30k/MS-COCO retrieval tasks. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership and regularized variants remain identical in Tables 1–3. The SimCLR/VICReg computational comparison and appendix comparisons with BYOL and covariance regularization are also retained.

E3.justification: Training budgets, architectures, batch sizes, augmentations, evaluation metrics, linear-probing procedures, and CLIP fine-tuning settings are unchanged. Appendix E.1 repairs a reference to existing settings without revising the protocol.

E4.justification: The collapse and uniformity experiments, coefficient analysis, projector and batch-size ablations, normalization comparison, seed-sensitivity study, and embedding analyses are unchanged, including the supplementary experiments in Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 retains seed 5, Table 9 retains mean and standard deviation reporting across five seeds, and Table 5 retains timing measurements averaged over 500 steps. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and experimental plots are retained. For example, standalone T-REGS remains at 91.3%/67.4% on CIFAR-10/100 in Table 1 and 80.3%/68.8% on ImageNet-100/1k in Table 2.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, mathematical statements, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A and G are unchanged. Section 4.2 replaces 'Theorem 4.6' with 'Corollary 4.6', correcting a reference label without altering the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about preventing dimensional collapse, promoting uniformity, theoretical guarantees on compact manifolds, and competitive standalone or auxiliary SSL performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sphere constraints, simplex-like embeddings, modality gaps, and the limitations of covariance-based regularization remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1, Table 6, Appendices C–D, and resource links retain the same implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, training-time, and access information. The repaired Appendix E.1 cross-reference points to existing details; revised allocation acknowledgments do not change the documented computing setup.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to contrastive learning, redundancy reduction, and Fang et al.'s uniformity regularization.

P1.justification: Limited editorial corrections replace 'Theorem 4.6' with 'Corollary 4.6' and the unresolved '??' in Appendix E.1 with 'Section C'. The acknowledgments add ANR/France 2030 support and revise GENCI allocation credits; the version stamp also changes. The narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is restyled with darker text and network blocks, thicker lines and arrows, and adjusted spacing. There is minor local page reflow, while the remaining figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability and navigation through the higher-contrast Figure 1, the corrected Corollary 4.6 reference, and replacement of the broken appendix reference with Section C. These are useful presentation repairs; the methods, scientific evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
